hero.intro: Two years building web-based ERP systems for construction, manufacturing and accounting teams, across 10+ business modules. Most recently, built an on-premise AI assistant that lets ERP customers query and modify data in plain language — a pipeline now used by 20+ customers daily, cutting inbound support questions by 30%. Deepest on Oracle, from PL/SQL to vector search. Claude Code and the BMAD-METHOD workflow are part of how I build now. Side projects include Debt Crusher, a Spring Boot app comparing three debt-payoff strategies (avalanche, snowball, minimum payments) through one shared amortization engine.

chat.title: Real-time Chat System for ERP
chat.tagline: A chat layer that lives inside the ERP, not beside it
chat.context: Gia Cat Technology Solutions · in-house ERP feature, used by external customers · sole developer
chat.description: A real-time chat layer built into the ERP platform, covering four kinds of conversation: one-to-one, group, threads attached to a specific ERP document, and channels that inherit the permission groups already defined in the ERP. The last two are the part an off-the-shelf messenger cannot do — a conversation that lives on a purchase order, and access that follows the permission data the system already holds.
responsibilities: Architected and built the full stack: Node.js backend, SSE-based message push, and the PL/SQL data layer
Wrote the browser chat client by hand in JavaScript, consuming the SSE event stream and rendering incoming messages without page reloads
Integrated Oracle CQN with a multi-database registry to detect row-level changes and fan out notifications
Designed the APEX to Node integration path through PL/SQL AJAX callbacks and UTL_HTTP with HMAC-SHA256 token authentication, keeping the internal server off the public network
Owned production deployment and operations with PM2 and custom start / stop shell scripts
Diagnosed and fixed two production bugs — a cross-schema message-delivery collision and a notification-badge desync — and flagged an unauthenticated broadcast endpoint as a security risk

Redesigned the browser client around a SharedWorker so every tab shares one connection instead of opening its own, cutting concurrent SSE connections by about 90% and eliminating a prior connection-limit issue
Built CLI verification scripts covering the REST endpoints, CQN callbacks, SSE streams and the connection registry

finance.title: Personal Finance Manager
finance.tagline: One binary serves the API and the React app that talks to it
finance.description: A personal finance app that turns income, fixed costs and a savings goal into one daily "safe-to-spend" number, so you always know what's left to spend without opening a spreadsheet.
responsibilities: Built the Go API on Gin: registration and login with bcrypt-hashed passwords and HS256 JWTs, with every row scoped to the signed-in user
Made one binary serve /api/* and the built SPA with history-mode fallback, so the whole app deploys as a single artifact
Added a "safe-to-spend" figure — income minus fixed costs, savings goal and spend-to-date, divided by days left in a configurable budget cycle — recomputed on every transaction
Triggered budget-threshold alerts (70/90/100% of a category's limit) inside the same database transaction as the expense that crossed it, surfaced as dismissible banners on the dashboard
Wrote the React and TypeScript client — dashboard, transactions table, budgets — with state carried by React Context instead of a state library

Ran the budgeting epic through a spec-driven review pass that caught real bugs before they shipped: a division that silently broke a "never go negative" guarantee, a timezone edge case in day-boundary math, and a double-counted transaction in threshold detection
Localised the entire interface in English and Vietnamese, including the ten default categories seeded at registration
Packaged it as a multi-stage Docker build and a Compose file covering app and database, with rate-limited auth endpoints and configurable CORS

debtCrusher.title: Debt Crusher
debtCrusher.tagline: Three payoff strategies compared side by side, refusing to project one that never finishes
debtCrusher.description: A debt payoff planner for anyone juggling multiple loans or cards who isn't sure which one to tackle first. It projects a full payoff timeline under three strategies (avalanche, snowball, minimum payments) so a user can compare and pick whichever gets them debt-free fastest — and refuses to show a plan that would never actually finish paying off.
responsibilities: Split the backend into five Maven modules along DDD lines — domain, infrastructure, application, controller, start — keeping the payoff math independent of Spring and JPA

Implemented avalanche, snowball, and minimum-only payoff strategies behind one interface and a factory, sharing a single amortization calculator so /payoff/compare returns all three side by side from one call
Added a PayoffNeverCompletesException so a projection where the minimum payment doesn't outpace accruing interest is rejected instead of returned as a schedule that runs forever
Built JWT registration and login with Resilience4j rate limiting on both endpoints to blunt brute-force attempts

Modeled seven domain exceptions (not-found, access-denied, invalid request, no active debts, user already exists, and others) so the API maps business failures to HTTP responses instead of leaking persistence errors
Wrote a demo-login path that seeds 20 sample debts on first backend start, so a visitor can try the planner without registering or entering their own data
Built the React and TypeScript client — login, debt list, payoff comparison — bilingual in English and Vietnamese, talking to the API over Axios
Set up local development with Docker Compose for MySQL and wrote separate production deploy docs with environment-variable templates

localAi.title: On-Premise AI Assistant for ERP
localAi.tagline: An agentic pipeline that reads ERP data or rewrites it — never both without asking first
localAi.context: Gia Cat Technology Solutions · in-house ERP feature, used by external customers · sole developer
localAi.description: A natural-language assistant embedded in the company's ERP, letting external customers query and modify their data in plain language instead of filing a support ticket. Every write needs explicit confirmation and lands in an audit log first, so a customer poking around their own data can't accidentally break anything. Self-initiated, researched and built end to end with Claude Code and the BMAD-METHOD workflow.
responsibilities: Designed the agentic dual-pipeline architecture: an intent router sends read requests to a RAG pipeline (bge-m3 embeddings, HNSW vector search) and write requests to a guarded Natural-Language-to-SQL flow with confirmation, audit logging and rollback
Traced a severe latency problem on CPU-only infrastructure to a security token that was breaking Ollama's prefix cache, using packet capture — then redesigned the flow into a single call to remove it
Evaluated the Natural-Language-to-SQL flow against 12 Vietnamese-language queries (100% correct) and 4 SQL-injection attempts before letting it touch real data
Indexed ERP data as vector embeddings in Oracle AI Database 26ai and wrote the PL/SQL packages the retrieval and write paths both call

about.title: About
paragraphs: I joined Gia Cat Technology Solutions as a back-end intern in 2024 and stayed on as a full stack developer. The work is internal business systems — ERP platforms for construction, manufacturing and accounting teams — where a feature is only finished when the people on the factory floor or in the accounts department can actually use it.

Most of what I do sits between the ERP and the world outside it. Pulling supplier invoices in from a third-party API, exposing the ERP's inventory data back out over REST, pushing database changes to a Node.js service in real time. The interesting problems are usually at the seams.

I am also the person on the team who gets asked to evaluate new technology and bring it into the system: push notifications, real-time notifications, the real-time chat platform, and — self-initiated — an on-premise AI assistant that lets external ERP customers query and modify data in plain language. Built end to end with Claude Code and the BMAD-METHOD workflow, it is now used by 20+ customers daily and has cut inbound support questions by 30%.
